page.layout: One page of text. An ornamental border at the top, then one block of Latin verse with a large initial, then the initials "A. H." below it. No margin notes. Faint show-through from the other side of the leaf is not transcribed.

p.i: Ast apage ambages; tu contrà fortior aude, Augustæ mentis semina prode tuæ. Crede mihi laus est, etiam hæc audere Geneuæ, Nec mage digna tibi, nec mage digna loco. Gratulor hanc mentem, quam si quoque cernere tentes, Ne te extra quæras, nam tibi totus ades. Est animus mensura sui, & certissima norma; Hunc adeat, quisquis se benè nosse volet.

page.notes: The large initial "A" is joined to "st" as "Ast"; the following word is set in small capitals ("ST"), which is read as "Ast". The border at the top is a printer's ornament and is not transcribed. The faint lines at the top ("DISPVT. THEOLOGICA") and in the lower half (the prose paragraph and the closing "SOLI DEO GLORIA.") are mirrored show-through from the reverse side and are left out; "SOLI DEO GLORIA." is faint enough that it could also be a printed closing line, so this is a doubtful decision. The sliver at the left edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. No page number, running head, catchword or signature is clearly printed on this leaf.
